verses.1: And Shmuel said to all of Israel, “Now I have heard your voices. You have spoken to me about everything you said to me. Now I will appoint a king for you.”
verses.2: And now, behold, the king is walking before you. I am old and have retired from public service. My sons are with you. I have walked before you since my youth until today.
verses.3: I have sinned against the LORD and against His Messiah. From whom did I take these things? From whom did I steal them? And whom did I oppress? Whom did I hate? From whom did I take these clothes and garments? My eyes are filled with tears, and I will answer you.
verses.4: And they said, “You have not punished us, nor taken anything from us. You have not taken anything from anyone.”
verses.5: And He said to them, “Let Jehovah and His Messiah be witness today that you have not found any merit in me.”
verses.6: And Shemuel said to the people, “Yahweh, who made Moses and Aaron, and who raised up your ancestors from the land of Egypt.”
verses.7: And now, stand up before Jehovah and be judged according to all the righteousness that Jehovah has done for you and for your ancestors.
verses.8: When Jacob came out of Egypt, your ancestors cried out to Jehovah. Then Jehovah sent Moses and Aaron to free your ancestors from Egypt. They brought them back to this place.
verses.9: And they forgot about Jehovah their God. They were sold into the hands of Sisera, commander of the army, and also into the hands of Jephthah and King Moab. They fought against them.
verses.10: They cried out to Jehovah and said, “We have sinned because we have abandoned Jehovah. We have worshiped our gods and idols. Now, save us from our enemies and let us serve you.”
verses.11: And Jehovah sent Jehu and Ben-hadad, and Elisha and Shemaiah. They defeated you from all around, and you were forced to take refuge in safety.
verses.12: And they saw that a serpent was the king of the children of Israel. They said to me, “Why does this serpent reign over us? After all, your God is the one who should rule over you.”
verses.13: And now, behold, the king whom you have chosen, whom you have selected… And now, behold, Jehovah has given you a king.
verses.14: If you fear Jehovah and serve him, and if you listen to his voice, then do not corrupt your mouth against Jehovah. Then both you and the king who rules over you will be blessed after Jehovah, your God.
verses.15: And if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD, and if you refuse to obey His commands, then the hand of the LORD will be upon you and also upon your ancestors.
verses.16: Even now, stand and see this great thing that Jehovah is doing for your eyes.
verses.17: Today, when the wheat is harvested, I will call upon Jehovah. He will give you plenty of food and knowledge. Then you will see that your sins are very great, since you have done things that go against Jehovah’s commands. He has given you a king to rule over you.
verses.18: And Shemuel called out to Jehovah. On that day, Jehovah gave him a rod and a staff. All the people were greatly afraid of Jehovah and of Shemuel.
verses.19: And all the people said to Samuel, “Pray to Jehovah your God for forgiveness for our sins. Do not let death come upon us because of all our evil deeds. Please give us a king.”
verses.20: And Shmuel said to the people, “Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil. But do not forget God. Serve God with all your hearts.”
verses.21: And do not remember that after the law, which does neither harm nor save, there will be no more law at all.
verses.22: For Jehovah will not bring his people back by his great name, because Jehovah has no desire to do this to you as a people.
verses.23: Also, I am sorry for my sins against God. I will no longer pray on your behalf. I have led you along the right and proper path.
verses.24: But they will see Jehovah and serve Him truly with all their hearts, because they will see that He has delivered them from their troubles.
verses.25: And if your enemies attack you, then your kings will also be defeated.
